message.content: Reviewing the final evidence: c1 and c2 are decisively rebutted by passing end-to-end probes across edge shapes, all group sizes, and shuffled g_idx (diffs ~1e-7 vs tolerance ≥0.01). c3 remains inconclusive only due to two probe construction bugs (uint16 arange/view issues), not any kernel evidence; moreover, the arithmetic itself is exact: (q−z) is a small integer and the scale is fp16-exact, so the fp32 product is exact and the single fp16 cast is the only rounding — matching the contract's H16 — and even a one-ulp decoded-weight difference would sit far below the 0.01+0.001·|target| tolerance given |D|≤0.5. No new material, testable, in-scope problem is exposed.

message.reasoning_content: Final review turn. c1 and c2 rebutted with strong evidence. c3 inconclusive (probe bugs), but note: the arithmetic analysis — (q-z) small int times fp16-exact scale is exact in fp32 (int up to 16, fp16 value has ≤11 significant bits, product ≤ 16*2^-14 fits in fp32 with plenty of precision; actually exact since fp16 has ≤11 bits and int ≤4 bits → ≤15 bits, exact in fp32). So the single fp16 round should match H16. Both failures were probe bugs, not kernel bugs. Also tolerance is 0.01+0.001|target| which is huge compared to fp16 rounding differences. No material new in-scope problem; c3 remains inconclusive but non-decisive given huge tolerance headroom. Default: record_no_new_claims.
